review_type: Targeted primary-source mechanism audit. Retrieval and mechanism design began before stage-e fitting, and the separate statistical plan was frozen before fitting. This long-form evidence document was subsequently compiled and corrected; its full completion before project-wide scoring is not asserted. Not a systematic review or a representative sample of the entire field.
main_conclusion: The candidate is an origin-conditioned discriminative regression with two signed damped trends and a standard regularized variable-projection estimator. The falsifiable domain claim is a conditional duration increment beyond static duration, conditional amplitude, free horizon heads and price/context interaction regression; its existence is not established by this literature audit.
mathematical_results_derived_here: A fixed64-history exponential state is a finite linear filter. With fixed rates and weights, each horizon is a restricted finite distributed-lag regression; its horizon-by-lag coefficient matrix has rank at most2.
The geometric cumulative response S_h(lambda) exactly matches the horizon shape of classical damped-trend forecasting, but the historical state updates differ from Holt.
Origin-fixed context and shared horizon coefficients do not establish rolling conditional-expectation coherence or causal identification.
At H1, duration scaling is confounded with amplitude in a sufficiently flexible comparator; the joint shape across horizons supplies the relevant restriction.
Ordered rates remove label permutations, not cancellation or weak identification.
The actual ridge penalty is alpha*||s(theta)*beta||^2 in unstandardized coordinates. Exact linear optimality does not guarantee a global nonlinear optimum.
The current ridge_interaction uses20 lagged price changes versus64 for response filters; this limit is disclosed rather than called identical full-history information.
